newsitem.title: USA: Tribune acquisition to boost revenues.
newsitem.headline: Tribune acquisition to boost revenues.

text.p: Tribune Corp expects Renaissance Communications Corp to contribute about $150 million to $160 million in revenues in 1997, said Jerry Agema, vice president-chief financial officer/operations for Tribune Broadcasting Co.
The $1.13 billion broadcasting acquisition was completed on Tuesday.

In the first quarter, Renaissance posted revenue growth in the "four to five percent range," Agema told analysts in a teleconference on Wednesday. But he said that pattern of growth in advertising bookings has slowed for April and May.
The Renaissance acquisition adds six television stations to Tribune's fold. It now has 16 network-affiliated TV stations along with superstation WGN-TV.
In 1996, Tribune Broadcasting posted operating revenues of $877 million. Tribune had total revenues of $2.41 billion.

Dennis FitzSimons, Tribune Broadcasting executive vice president, said WGN-TV is positioned for growth. "As a superstation outside the Chicago market, WGN is a $50 million (annual) revenue business that we think can double in the near future," said FitzSimons as its reach expands.
